comparator.name: Nederlands, Europees en Internationaal Recht
comparator.academicYear: Published indicative 2027–2028 prospectus curriculum for each of the three listed years; later cohorts may change
comparator.sourceNotes: Radboud lists 60 EC of required legal study in each year of the standard pathway. Its separate French–Dutch legal translation specialisation modifies the second year and is not combined here. The third year includes 56 EC of required courses and one 4-EC restricted choice; Philosophy of Law is one permitted choice. The 0-EC first-year tutorial is outside the credited curriculum. The official year pages call the 2027–2028 listing provisional for prospective students and do not promise these exact courses for a Fall 2026 entrant.

alternatives.label: Law, European institutions and international justice
alternatives.concept: A law-led curriculum spanning constitutional, criminal, private, EU and international law, together with political institutions, legal argument and the social conditions of justice. It has substantial legal coverage but cannot reproduce Radboud’s sustained Dutch civil and procedural law sequence or its required legal thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains six substantive law courses plus law foundations, European and international politics, cross-border commerce and justice; the label describes this combination without claiming a Dutch qualifying law degree.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes all formally dependent 200/300-level law courses; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law. Comparative politics and sociology foundations precede advanced EU politics and social theory, and all course offerings and formal prerequisites are satisfied.

candidates.label: French–Dutch legal translation
candidates.reason: The separate specialist route requires French language proficiency and translation of legal texts. The UCR workbook offers no French language or French–Dutch legal translation sequence; general stylistics and Dutch cannot sustain a distinct 24-course translation curriculum.

candidates.label: European and international legal advocacy
candidates.reason: The strongest available UCR legal, EU, international and rhetoric courses already anchor the closest-match programme. A second advocacy label would retain that core and reshuffle complementary courses without changing its academic priority or producing a substantively different legal curriculum.

selection.assessment: One 24-course law-led response captures the Dutch, EU and international law core with explicitly limited Dutch procedural and civil-law depth. The French–Dutch translation specialisation is not feasible with the current UCR course offer; legal advocacy is already substantively integrated into the first alternative and cannot justify a distinct second curriculum.

notes.text: Radboud offers a three-year Dutch, EU and international law sequence with extensive Dutch private and procedural law and a required legal thesis. UCR combines selected law courses with politics, society and communication, but does not reproduce Radboud’s depth or professional legal qualification pathway.
